articles.title: Claressa Shields not upset Katie Taylor fight didn't happen and sends retirement message to Irish great
articles.summary: Claressa Shields and Amanda Serrano both wished Katie Taylor a happy retirement as the Irish great prepares for the final bout of her professional career this weekend; Shields played down the idea she was upset the two never shared the ring, praising Taylor's historic career.
articles.body:
Taylor enters her farewell bout this weekend when she takes on Flora Pili in an undisputed super-lightweight world title clash at Dublin's Croke Park in front of more than 80,000 fans.

The Irish icon, a two-weight undisputed world champion and Olympic gold medallist, will hang up her gloves widely-recognised as the greatest fighter in female boxing history.

Five-weight world champion Shields has arguably become the closest rival to Taylor's reputation at the pinnacle of the sport.

"Am I number one? I have always shared that with Katie," Shields told Sky Sports. "Me and her joke and say we're 1A and 1B, because we're both just that good.

"I'm not a person that really cares about the pound for pound list. I know that I've been number one or two on there for the past five, six years.

"But I know that Katie, she's a great fighter. She's a warrior. And I wish her a happy retirement. And I hope that she gets a big knock out her last fight."

Shields, a three-time undisputed world champion, has fought at heavier weight-classes than Taylor, hence the pair never crossing paths in their respective glittering careers.

"I'm not mad that it didn't happen," said Shields. "We had weight classes for a reason. And I respect her greatness and she respects mine.

"I beat the best in my divisions, and she's beat the best in her divisions. I respect that. So no, I'm not upset that we never got to fight.

"I am happy to be able to watch her and her greatness. She's done the same for me. And like I said, I wish her a happy retirement."

Taylor enters Saturday's contest 25-1 having suffered her only professional career defeat against Chantelle Cameron in May 2023.

Among her highlights is a trilogy of wins over Puerto Rican great Amanda Serrano, the first of which saw the pair compete in the first ever women's boxing match to headline at Madison Square Garden.

"I think Katie's done what she wanted to do. I think this is her time," Serrano told Sky Sports.

"You can feel it, I've been 17 years in the sport. It's about time.

"Me and Katie, we've made lots of money together, we made history together and big fights. I think she's done enough for the sport. She deserves this homecoming fight.

"I'm happy for her. I just can't wait to see her future when she's retired with her family life and all that good stuff. She deserves it."

articles.title: Katie Taylor ready to go 'one more time' as glittering career ends at Croke Park with dreams of being undisputed again
articles.summary: Katie Taylor weight in at 139.6lbs for her final fight - an undisputed super-lightweight showdown against unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in Dublin on Saturday night, in front of 80,000 fans - "I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years"
articles.body:
Taylor will aim to retire as a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on unbeaten France's Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who weighed in at 139.6lbs for the super-lightweight showdown compared to Pili's 139.9lbs, has pretty much done it all in boxing.

Her accolades including winning Olympic gold in London in 2012 and, along with Amanda Serrano, becoming the first woman to headline a fight card at New York's iconic Madison Square ‌Garden.

She also avenged her sole pro defeat, against Chantelle Cameron.

But she has never fought at Croke Park before - until now.

'This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for'

While fight week, quite rightly, has seen the great and good of boxing and beyond praise Taylor's career, hail the inspiration she has been and discuss the legacy she will leave, the woman herself is not looking beyond Pili.

Speaking shortly after hitting the scales on Friday evening, the Bray Bomber, said: "My mind is focused on the fight. I have a job to do against a very tough challenger.

"I have built my reputation on always taking the tough fights, so why treat my last fight any differently? This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for. Let's go one more time."

Taylor did, though, turn to address her fans at the weigh-in, many of whom will also be rooting for her inside the stadium this weekend.

"I am blown away. I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years

"You guys have carried me throughout the Olympics and my whole career. Thank you so much. I am so grateful.

"I am so excited. I have been dreaming about this for the last few years and I am one day away from ending my career in a dream venue in front of all these amazing people."

'Katie is an absolute hero to so many people'

Former world champion Carl Frampton, speaking on DAZN , feels the lure of a bout at Saturday's prolonged Taylor's time as an active fighter.

He said: "She has completed the sport but I think one of the reasons she held on was the dream of fighting at Croke Park. She has finally got it.

"Katie is an absolute hero to so many people, an inspiration. It is a perfect way to finish - but she has to win first and we can't rule out Pili who is a very good fighter."

Three-weight world champion Mikaela Mayer added: "Katie has always been very true to her word.

"If she says this is her last fight, I believe it to be. If she wants to come back, I would not be upset about it. We'd love to see her again.

"I am benefitting off of her hard work and everything she has helped create for the women in this sport. I am sad as I had always hoped to share the ring with Katie."

articles.title: ‘Papai te ama’: homem se emociona ao deixar filho no estágio; vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: Um vídeo simples de 16 segundos que mostra a relação afetuosa entre Heleno e Daniel Duarte encantou milhares de pessoas nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: O filho é estagiário de medicina em Fortaleza. Um vídeo de 16 segundos que mostra a relação afetuosa entre Heleno e Daniel Duarte encantou milhares de pessoas nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Seria inapropriado tentar reduzir a um só motivo o porquê viralizou um vídeo que mostra o promotor de vendas Heleno Duarte deixar o filho, Daniel Duarte, no primeiro dia de estágio em um hospital de Fortaleza . Os 16 segundos de filmagem representam apenas um recorte da relação afetuosa entre os dois. O carinho e orgulho na voz do pai , no entanto, foram suficientes para render ao vídeo quase 1 milhão de visualizações.

Daniel é estudante de medicina na Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC). Ele está no quarto semestre e, no dia 21 de setembro, começou a primeira experiência profissional, como estagiário do Hospital do Coração , unidade de saúde pública, do bairro Messejana, em Fortaleza.

“Eu me emocionei na hora, quase chorei em cima da moto. Quando eu saí, eu só agradeci a Deus”, comentou Heleno, que tem 49 anos.

“Ele estava tão bonito. Eu já venho alegre [desde o ano passado], porque essa aprovação dele com 17 anos em medicina, ele veio de uma escola pública. Pra mim, isso aí já foi uma grande riqueza”, se orgulhou o pai.

Os dois são moradores da comunidade Rosalina, no bairro Parque Dois Irmãos, em Fortaleza. Daniel fez o ensino médio na Escola de Ensino Médio Professora Maria Gonçalves, que faz parte da rede pública do estado, no bairro Boa Vista-Castelão.

Vídeo viraliza após pai se emocionar ao deixar filho no primeiro dia de estágio em hospital de Fortaleza. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Heleno decidiu filmar o momento e, sem grandes pretensões, publicou no próprio perfil do Instagram, que, antes, tinha no máximo 300 visualizações por publicação.

A repercussão do momento familiar pegou ambos de surpresa. “Eu não faço a menor ideia, é sério” , disse Daniel, que tem 19 anos, ao ser perguntado se imagina porque o vídeo viralizou.

“Eu nem esperava que ele fosse gravar aquele vídeo, porque ele começou a gravar e eu pensei: ‘ah, deve ser só mais um vídeo que ele vai colocar no grupo da família, postando nos status do WhatsApp’. Eu só pensei: ‘ah, tá bom’”, lembrou o universitário.

Heleno disse que soube que o vídeo estava repercutindo ao chegar no trabalho e ser avisado por colegas. “Quando eu cheguei [no trabalho], começaram a falar que o vídeo viralizou. Eu não sabia nem o que era viralizar ”, disse.

Pai e filho, Heleno Duarte e Daniel Duarte, durante evento do curso de medicina da UFC. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O carinho e o orgulho expressados tão fortemente no vídeo, em que o pai diz explicitamente amar o filho , chamou a atenção especialmente quando se tem ainda a figura paterna/masculina como “fechada, sem sentimento”. Heleno se orgulha em ser ponto fora da curva.

“Eu sempre fui esse pai, sempre acompanhei ele na escola, sempre falava com ele. Graças a Deus, pra mim ele é um menino muito bom, respeitador, educado, entendeu? Só elogio ao meu filho, graças a Deus”, declarou o promotor de vendas.

“Não tem dinheiro nenhum que pague isso. Eu posso dizer que eu sou o homem mais rico do mundo”, complementou.

O orgulho é refletido e sentido pelo jovem universitário. “É uma relação de muita proximidade, a gente se levanta, conversa, logo de manhã cedo. Ele trabalha, eu vou para a minha faculdade, tem vezes que ele consegue me deixar, tem outras vezes que não”, comentou Daniel.

“Ele sempre vai me aconselhando, conversando comigo. É muito bom. Geralmente a gente se encontra mais pela noite, que é quando eu volto da faculdade e ele volta do trabalho. A gente conversa, é muito bom, é uma relação muito boa”, agradeceu o filho.

articles.title: Norma Dumont makes her bout personal with NSFW move at Ailin Perez in wild UFC Vegas 121 faceoff
articles.summary: Norma Dumont had little interest in keeping Friday’s UFC Vegas 121 faceoff routine.

Perez performed her trademark twerking celebration during the faceoff, prompting Dumont to pull the co**oms from her shorts and throw them toward her rival.“You need this,” Dumont said with a smile.Norma Dumont tosses co**oms and cash at Ailin Perez in unexpected UFC scenePerez then picked up the items, but Dumont was not finished. articles.title: Oktagon 94: The MMA fighter helping Brighton and filling stadiums in Frankfurt
articles.summary: From helping Brighton with set pieces to fighting in front of nearly 60,000 people - meet MMA star Christian Eckerlin, who competes at Oktagon 94 in Frankfurt on Saturday.
articles.body:
Christian Eckerlin laughs modestly when asked if he feels he has contributed to Brighton's success.

Last season, the 39-year-old MMA fighter was brought in by the Premier League club to help with their training for set-pieces.

Eckerlin was a professional footballer in Germany before transitioning to MMA, and says he taught Brighton players "wrestling, head control, hip control, and how to push back against opponents".

Days before this interview with Eckerlin took place, the Seagulls moved up to third in the Premier League after beating champions and set-piece kings Arsenal 3-0.

Eckerlin is quick to play down the impact of his advice for the Brighton players, but admits his training "opened doors" for them.

"The Premier League is more physical, more aggressive, and they don't know how to use their body," Eckerlin told BBC Sport.

"Brighton sent me videos of how they defend, and they did nothing with their hips and arms.

"I taught them first in the weightlifting room, then the pitch, and it worked. This is what I did, I opened doors for them."

Eckerlin was a professional footballer from 2005 to 2009, playing for SV Darmstadt in the third tier of German football at the peak of his career.

As a youngster, Eckerlin always wanted to play for the team he supports, Eintracht Frankfurt, but believed his dream was over when he left the sport.

Little did he know that MMA, and specifically European promotion Oktagon, would help make his dream of performing there come true.

In 2024, Eckerlin beat fellow German Christian Jungwirth at Frankfurt's Deutsche Bank Park in front of nearly 60,000 fans in the most-attended MMA event of the year.

On Saturday, Eckerlin returns to the stadium also known as the Waldstadion for a second time to face the Czech Republic's David Kozma at Oktagon 94 with nearly 60,000 expected once again.

"It was my first dream, when I was in the Waldstadion when I was six or seven with my uncle. It was the dream for me to play there but I thought the fire went out," says Eckerlin.

"I cannot tell you in words what this means to me. The biggest thing in my career. And now for the second time... crazy.

"I'm at the end of my career, I'm 39, so this is maybe my last fight. There's no better way to stop fighting in my backyard, you know."

'My promise to my late son is what keeps me alive'

'When I retire I'll see what I did for MMA in Germany'

Eckerlin grew up in a small town outside Frankfurt called Erbach and says football "was his first passion".

During his youth career he played against stars such as Bastian Schweinsteiger and Mats Hummels, but ended up leaving football at the age of 20 after a disagreement with his coaches.

"I got a little bit crazy and partied with friends. But my popularity went down with the coaches," said Eckerlin.

"They said 'you cannot do this'. But I was young, nobody was on my side to say 'calm down and do your thing'. So I said 'OK, I'm going'."

Eckerlin played at left-back but admits he "wasn't a technical guy" before joking he was more of a fighter on the pitch.

He knows Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler through a friend who used to play with him in Munich.

It was Hurzeler who invited Eckerlin over to Brighton, where he spent three days with the players.

Eckerlin says all the players did well learning the MMA techniques he taught them, but Danny Welbeck, James Milner and Lewis Dunk "had the feeling for it".

Football remains the most popular sport in Germany, but Eckerlin says he helped grow his following after switching to MMA via his YouTube channel.

He says the fanfare in Frankfurt is "crazy", with fans always wanting to take pictures with him, but adds he is equally as well known in large cities such as Berlin and Hamburg.

With nearly 60,000 fans expected again for his fight on Saturday, the show is likely to be the most well-attended MMA event of the year once again.

Before what Eckerlin describes as probably the final fight of his 26-fight career, he takes a moment to reflect on the impact he's had on MMA in Germany.

"I love this sport, and I push the sport more than everybody or anybody before in this country," says Eckerlin.

"After my career, when I look back, I think then I will realise, what I do for the sport, or for MMA in Germany. But now I'm fully focused, and there's no time to think about the things in the past."

articles.title: Javon Walton: The boxer who accidentally became an actor
articles.summary: Euphoria star Javon Walton discusses his boxing roots, acting career and Saturday's fight with UFC great Henry Cejudo.
articles.body:
Javon Walton has spent much of his life performing under bright lights. Sometimes there is a camera in front of him. At other times, there is an opponent trying to punch him back.

To millions, the 20-year-old is better known as Ashtray - the tattooed teenage drug dealer in hit HBO TV drama Euphoria.

But on Saturday, American Walton headlines a Misfits Boxing event in Miami against former two-weight UFC champion and Olympic wrestling gold medallist Henry Cejudo.

You could be forgiven for thinking this is another celebrity trying his hand at boxing in an era of influencer fights and crossover events. But Walton had "zero interest in acting" as a young child - boxing was his first love.

"My parents were boxing fans and when it was on HBO on Saturdays, I would watch it with them," he tells BBC Sport.

"I practically begged my dad to take me to a gym and when I was four years old he finally took me."

Walton has since amassed 85 amateur bouts, twice won silver at the Junior Olympics and is unbeaten as a professional with three wins and a draw. He is signed to Jake Paul and Nakisa Bidarian's Most Valuable Promotions.

Walton competed at a high level in gymnastics after following his sister into the sport, but boxing remained his obsession.

It was the sweet science, somewhat ironically, which eventually opened the door to a completely different form of performance.

Walton appeared on Steve Harvey's television show aged 11 to showcase his boxing ability, throwing combinations on the pads before also demonstrating his gymnastics skills with a backflip.

Casting director Jennifer Venditti saw the appearance and contacted his family about auditioning for Euphoria.

"I was like, 'OK, why not?'" Walton says. "And that just led to one opportunity after another."

What started by accident grew into a substantial acting career. Walton went on to appear in Amazon drama Utopia and Netflix series The Umbrella Academy, and even found himself working alongside the man behind cinema's most famous boxer Rocky Balboa, Sylvester Stallone, in Samaritan.

"I found my love in that space," Walton says. "I look at that as an outlet where I can tap into my emotions because you can't do that in boxing."

The harder challenge now is finding room for both careers. Walton says filming can take him away for six months, while preparing to fight demands an eight-week camp and complete focus.

"My goal is to see how well I can balance both but that's easier said than done," he says. "I kind of have to pick one to focus on."

For now, that focus is Cejudo. The 39-year-old won Olympic freestyle wrestling gold in 2008 before becoming a UFC champion in two weight divisions, but Saturday will be his professional boxing debut.

The bout, which Walton accepted at less than two weeks' notice after Cejudo's original opponent withdrew, has been sanctioned by the Florida State Commission and will count towards their professional records.

"You have to have a level of respect," Walton says. "But at the same time he's stepping into unmarked territory - my field and something I've done my whole life.

"On the mat it would be a different story, but this is the ring."

In Walton's corner will be the man who first took him to a gym as a four-year-old - his father and trainer, DJ.

"What was beautiful about our journey was we got to grow together," Walton says.

"While I was learning how to be a fighter at a young age, he was learning the coaching side. The way I look at it is we're the pilot and co-pilot. He's a head coach who happens to be my dad. I want to do right by us and not just for me."

articles.title: WOW 32 Sevilla, historia por hacer e historias por contar
articles.standfirst: La promotora líder de MMA en España regresa a la capital andaluza con el primer cinturón femenino de su historia
articles.summary: La promotora líder de MMA en España regresa a la capital andaluza con el primer cinturón femenino de su historia
articles.body: Este sábado WOW FC regresa a Sevilla con WOW 32, un evento con un color especial en el que Sara Viéitez (3-2) y Hanna Palmquist (3-0) tienen una cita con la historia, ya que se disputarán en la categoría de peso paja el primer cinturón femenino de la historia de WOW FC. Además, también formarán parte de la cartelera otros nombres a tener en cuenta por lo mucho que pueden dar que hablar en un futuro no muy lejano. Obviamente, el foco principal estará centrado en Viéitez y Palmquist por todo lo que hay en juego. Ambas se han ganado a pulso este combate titular con dos victorias en sus dos combates en la promotora, y en el caso de la peleadora española se ha convertido en una peleadora franquicia. En su último combate en WOW Lisboa el pasado mayo noqueó a Eduarda Santos y se convirtió en la primera peleadora que recibe un bono de la noche en WOW FC, por lo que 2026 puede ser el año en el que haga historia por partida doble. Palmquist es todo lo opuesto a Sara, fría como el hielo y parca en palabras. Su único objetivo es pasar cuanto antes la Fight Week para que llegue el sábado y poder lograr su cometido. En su etapa amateur fue campeona IMMAF y todavía no conoce la derrota, por lo que Viéitez tendrá en frente a la rival más difícil de su carrera en un duelo del que puede salir la primera gran superestrellande la promotora. Sin embargo, el espectáculo no se ciñe únicamente al combate estelar. En el co estelar estará presente Pepe Torres (10-1), que regresa a WOW FC como una de las mayores promesas del panorama español. El antiguo sparring de Ilia Topuria ha tenido unos últimos meses convulsos en los que le ha pasado de todo, por lo que esta es una oportunidad de oro para brillar y dar un paso de gigante de cara a consagrarse y acercarse a su sueño de ser campeón de la UFC. Eso sí, para ello tendrá que superar a un Jefferson Vargas (5-2) que intentará dar la mayor sorpresa de la velada. También se podrá ver de vuelta a Daniel Ladero (4-3) tras su controversial combate titular ante Enoc Solves en WOW Valencia, que acabó en un 'no contest'. El peleador español se medirá al polaco Przemysław Dzwoniarek (4-3), a sabiendas de que el ganador tendrá prácticamente asegurada una oportunidad por el cinturón de peso semipesado. El combate del pueblo será el que protagonicen Jeffry Batista (6-1) y Junior Hernandez (6-1-1), dos de los mayores talentos de la cartelera. Batista entrena en Barcelona y vuelve a la promotora -no compite desde amateur- para consolidarse como una estrella en el panorama nacional, aunque para ello tendrá que superar a un peleador que tiene un gran bagaje y suma siete combates consecutivos sin perder. Además, Pablo Colado (2-0) buscará mantener el invicto frente a su gente ante Vitor Enrique (3-1), mientras que Enrique Kakulov (0-0) debutará en amateur en MMA con todas las expectativas puestas en él. El peleador español llega a WOW FC con el cartel de campeón de España en boxeo y Kickboxing, y su objetivo es finalizar pronto a Christian Berrocal (3-2) y dar el salto a profesional a final de año para acercarse al título de peso gallo cuanto antes.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight could be off, says Tyson Fury
articles.summary: Tyson Fury says his long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua in December is in jeopardy.
articles.body:
Tyson Fury says his long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua in December is in jeopardy because of a row between rival promoters.

The bout was announced earlier this week following years of failed negotiations, with the pair set to fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.

The event, which will be broadcast on Netflix, was confirmed as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and UFC president Dana White, but this appears to be the sticking point.

Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, has been at odds with White in recent months, and says the UFC head's involvement is a breach of their contract.

Fury says Matchroom promoter Hearn's reluctance to work with White is putting the fight in doubt.

"Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight. They're saying they're not going to fight now," Fury posted on Instagram.

"It's mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. He's making up a million different things and threatening we're not going to fight.

"Now you've got Turki Alalshikh finding alternative real men who will fight at the drop of a hat. Eddie Hearn has cost us the biggest fight in boxing history."

Hearn has been publicly feuding with UFC president White since the launch of Zuffa Boxing earlier this year.

Speaking to IFL TV, Hearn said White's involvement in the promotion of the Fury and Joshua fight "ain't happening", despite Netflix's news release.

"Dana White cannot be involved with this fight promotion. Netflix clearly didn't get the memo. No-one talks to each other," said Hearn.

"Then Netflix say the fight is in conjunction with Dana White. Now we have to go through that process and deal with it. It's a little bit annoying but as I've shown through the UK battle that we won, we stand by our contracts."

Fury's promoter Frank Warren said White was influential in securing the deal with Netflix after the fight was confirmed.

Fury's claim the bout could be off follows his post on social media earlier this month suggesting that Joshua, 36, was backing out of the fight, before calling for a third match-up with Oleksandr Usyk.

There was no official statement from Hearn or Warren in the news release sent out by Netflix to announce the fight.

BBC Sport has contacted Matchroom, Warren's company Queensberry Promotions, The Ring and Netflix for comment.

The dispute between Hearn and White is the latest stumbling block following years of failed negotiations around the fight.

In 2020, the two camps agreed the basis of a two-fight deal. In 2021, contracts were signed for an undisputed heavyweight contest, only for Deontay Wilder's successful arbitration case to force Fury into a third fight with the American.

Then, in 2022, Joshua accepted a 60-40 split to challenge Fury, but that attempt also fell apart.

Fury and Joshua finally signed contracts for the bout earlier this year, with the date and venue confirmed this week.

articles.title: UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje admits he may never have beaten Khabib Nurmagomedov despite winning first round
articles.summary: Justin Gaethje has admitted he still does not know whether he could have beaten Khabib Nurmagomedov in their UFC 254 fight.
articles.body: Justin Gaethje has admitted he still does not know whether he could have beaten Khabib Nurmagomedov in their UFC 254 fight. Gaethje won the opening round on two of the three judges’ scorecards. However, the UFC lightweight champion said the effort required to survive Khabib’s pressure left him with little energy for what followed.“I wasn’t gonna win that fight after the first round,” Gaethje said. He said that winning the first round had taken everything out of him. Khabib eventually took Gaethje down early in the second round and submitted him with a triangle choke at 1:34. The loss was Gaethje’s only fight against the undefeated Russian.Justin Gaethje says Khabib Nurmagomedov’s pressure changed the fightJustin Gaethje entered UFC 254 as one of the biggest threats to Khabib Nurmagomedov’s undefeated record. The fight took place on October 24, 2020, on Fight Island in Abu Dhabi. Khabib was defending his UFC lightweight title.Gaethje started strongly. He attacked Khabib’s lead leg with powerful kicks and looked to keep the fight standing. His striking gave Nurmagomedov problems during the opening minutes.The first round was extremely demanding for both fighters. Khabib continued moving forward and applying Nurmagomedov. He also secured a takedown late in the round and moved into a dominant position.Despite that, two judges scored the round 10-9 for Gaethje. Derek Cleary gave the round to Khabib.Gaethje has now opened up on how much energy he had used during those five minutes. He said on One Night With Steiny, “I beat Khabib in the first round on two of the three scorecards, and it took everything in my body to win that first round. I wasn’t going to win after that. I think it could have been just his pressure.”The second round showed exactly what Gaethje was talking about.Gaethje opened the round with another heavy leg kick. Khabib timed it perfectly. He caught the kick and immediately closed the distance.Gaethje tapped, but referee Jason Herzog did not immediately see it. The submission continued until Gaethje lost consciousness at 1:34 of the second round.The victory moved Khabib’s professional record to 29-0. He then shocked the MMA world by announcing his retirement. Khabib removed his gloves and placed them inside the Octagon.The fight also became an important part of Khabib’s legacy. He officially lost only two rounds on judges’ scorecards during his professional career.The first came against Conor McGregor at UFC 229. McGregor won the third round on all three scorecards before Khabib finished him by submission in the fourth.The second was the opening round against Gaethje.Khabib went on to retire undefeated after UFC 254. Gaethje, meanwhile, continued competing at the top level of the lightweight division.For Gaethje, the question of whether a rematch would have produced a different result remains unanswered. articles.standfirst: Afirma que el duelo, previsto para diciembre, corre peligro por la disputa entre Eddie Hearn, promotor de Joshua, y Dana White
articles.summary: Afirma que el duelo, previsto para diciembre, corre peligro por la disputa entre Eddie Hearn, promotor de Joshua, y Dana White
articles.body: El esperado cara a cara entre Tyson Fury y Anthony Joshua, ya con fecha oficial, vuelve a estar en el alambre. Dentro de la liturgia que suele acompañar este tipo de combates, Fury ha encendido las alarmas al comentar que el duelo corre peligro de celebrarse por la disputa entre Eddie Hearn, promotor de Joshua, y Dana White, uno de los dos artífices de la pelea junto con The Ring, propiedad del influyente empresario saudí Turki Alalshikh. Alalshikh oficializó la denominada ‘batalla de Gran Bretaña’ para el 11 de diciembre de 2026 en Cardiff, en el Principality Stadium, y retransmitida por Netflix. La presencia de White, presidente de la UFC, como promotor junto al empresario saudí, no es aceptada por Eddie Hearn, enfrentado con White desde hace meses. El mandamás de Matchoroom considera que supone un incumplimiento de su contrato. Fury afirma que la reticencia del promotor de Matchroom, Hearn, a trabajar con White está poniendo en duda la celebración del combate. "Anthony Joshua y Eddie Hearn están intentando retirarse de esta pelea. Dicen que ya no van a pelear. Cobardes. Les he dado todo lo que querían", publicó Fury en Instagram al conocerse las reticencias de Hearn. "Tiene que ver principalmente con el ego de Eddie Hearn. Se está inventando un millón de cosas diferentes y amenaza con que no vamos a pelear. Ahora tenemos a Turki Alalshikh buscando hombres de verdad que estén dispuestos a pelear en cualquier momento. Eddie Hearn nos ha costado la pelea más importante de la historia del boxeo. ¡Qué payaso!", explicó Fury. La disputa entre Hearn y White tiene su origen en la puesta en marcha a principio de año de Zuffa Boxing, la empresa fundada por el presidente de la UFC y respaldada por financiación saudí para promover combates de boxeo. En declaraciones a IFL TV, Hearn afirmó que la participación de White en la promoción de la pelea entre Fury y Joshua "no se producirá", a pesar de que así lo anunció Netflix: "Dana White no puede estar involucrado en la promoción de esta pelea. Es evidente que Netflix no se enteró. Nadie se comunica entre sí", dijo Hearn. "Entonces Netflix dice que la pelea es en colaboración con Dana White. Ahora tenemos que pasar por ese proceso y lidiar con ello. Es un poco molesto, pero como demostré en la batalla que ganamos en el Reino Unido, cumplimos con nuestros contratos". Joshua y Fury tienen prevista una rueda de prensa en Londres este miércoles 30 de septiembre.

articles.title: Johnny Fisher: 'The knocks, cuts and scars, they can build you. Don’t let them break you, let them build you'
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher fights Michael Pirotton Saturday night at the Copper Box Arena: "When you hear that crowd roar you can let it either overtake your brain and frazzle it, or channel everything"; Watch Zuffa Boxing 11 live on Sky Sports from 7pm
articles.body:
The hugely popular "Romford Bull" has lost when he expected to win. He's struggled at times, he can turn a tune-up fight into a brawl.

He is undeniably a heavy puncher and is increasingly improving on how he makes use of that strength and power.

He is aware of something else too. Heavyweight boxing is different. With men this big, punching this hard, anyone can lose. It means anyone can win too.

The very best prospects can still suffer surprise defeat. The heavyweight underdog can always spring a surprise.

"There's something special about the boxing world where two big gentlemen go into the ring and they really lay it all to bare for everyone to see. So that's why people tune in," Fisher told Sky Sports .

"Enjoy the journey, enjoy the ride. That's all it is. My ride might end with me fighting for an English title or a British title or having a big fight at the Copper Bosh against a hard opponent and it falling all apart but I'll give 110 per cent every single time. That's what it's about."

He's fighting at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday night, live on Sky Sports , against Belgium's Michael Pirotton, who has lost twice before but only against unbeaten opponents. Pirotton has never been dropped or stopped before, unlike Fisher.

The Englishman however believes his setbacks will ultimately enhance him.

"If it was easy, there'd be a lot more blokes doing it," he said.

"All of them little knocks, them cuts and them scars, they can build you. Don't let them break you, let them build you."

He will have his tremendous fanbase, the "Romford Bull Army" urging him on at the Copper Box. Having that kind of support is something unique. Pirotton wants to use that pressure against the local hero. But Fisher insists that is not going to happen.

"It's dealing with the pressure of them big circumstances. I've been in front of arenas of thousands of people for a long time now, so I can deal with that," he said.

"When you hear that roar you can let it either overtake your brain and frazzle it, or channel everything. You've just got to channel it and use it to focus you.

"That roar when you hear it, it's like a genuine roar and they make noise throughout the whole fight."

For him it's not the kind of pressure you might expect. He knows he has their support win or lose. In that sense he is unburdened. "You've got to view it as a privilege that these people come out and support you," he said.

"These people are really genuine and they want to come out and see me do well. They turn out no matter what. So that adds another level of a different pressure. I've been wrestling with that thought in my head. It's a bit of an oxymoronic thought."

He is determined to show the improvement in his ringcraft, but adds: "I'm done with the days of trying to prove myself to anyone. Who am I trying to prove anything to?

"To try and impress human beings you're doing the wrong thing. All you've got to do is live life the way you think you should live it and be kind to people, give people enjoyment, give people entertainment and be a genuine person and try your hardest.

"Try your best and that's all you can do."

Craig Richards will take on Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic in a top class light-heavyweight 10-rounder as the chief support to Fisher vs Pirotton.

Both Richards and Kalajdzic have operated at the highest level. "Hot Rod" boxed Artur Beterbiev, the destructive light-heavyweight wrecking machine, in a 2019 IBF world title challenge. In his most recent fight, Kalajdzic picked himself up from the deck twice to take out former champion Oleksandr Gvozdyk.

Richards boxed Dmitry Bivol in 2021, a performance that looks better and better after Bivol went on to prove himself the best in the division and become undisputed champion.

"The biggest thing I learned from that fight, I was a little bit disappointed that I didn't go through the gears as much as I could," Richards reflected of his fight with Bivol.

"You saw the interview before the Beterbiev first fight and they said: 'Who was your hardest fight?' He [Bivol] said: 'Actually a guy, Craig Richards, from England.' He said: 'It looks like it wasn't that to you lot, but there was a lot of thinking going on in there.'

"I think sometimes as a boxer there's so much that comes into account rather than just trading punches in there. Timing, traps, IQ, and at that elite level, I think, you will understand and they understand what's going on in there."

He wants a second shot at the champion. "I saw Bivol a couple of years ago and he said to me :'I know I'm going to see you again' and I said to him: '100 per cent,'" Richards told Sky Sports . "He knows we're going to meet again."

Richards wants to fight the very best, because that's where he feels he belongs: "If I leave this sport and I don't show everyone how good I am it will be very disappointing."

Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton headline Zuffa Boxing 11, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.

articles.title: Radivoje Kalajdzic drops Craig Richards to hand him dramatic hometown defeat at the Copper Box Arena in London
articles.summary: Radivoje Kalajdzic puts Craig Richards down in the last round as he hands him a homecoming defeat; Lee Cutler defuses hard-punching Louis Greene and prospects Kayla Allen and Alex MacMillan impress; Watch Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Richards, fighting in his home city for the first time since 2024, was looking to force his way back into the world title picture.

But "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic savagely supplanted him, taking a unanimous decision after handing Richards a heavy knockdown in the closing seconds of the contest.

In their tremendous 10-round battle, Richards was badly wobbled in the sixth round, only for "Spider" to come back with fierce determination himself.

Just as Richards was dominating the last round, lashing "Hot Rod" from one set of ropes to another with well-judged body hooks and hard crosses to the head, Kalajdzic counter-attacked viciously.

He darted in with a combination, knocking punches against Richards' head. Then in the closing seconds of the fight, Kalajdzic landed a stunning right, that toppled Richards all the way over.

He flopped onto his side. Somehow Richards rose, but his legs were shaking beneath him. The bell rang to save him from a cold finish but Kalajdzic won unanimously, 97-92 for all three judges

Lee Cutler's nickname might be "Chaos" but he was all about control as he defused the threat of Louis Greene over 10 rounds.

Greene is heavy-handed, and after a quiet start he clipped the Bournemouth man, hurting Cutler and momentarily buckling his legs.

Cutler recovered himself, reeling off a right of his own to start the fourth round. He smacked in a one-two but Greene stood close in hacking at Cutler with punches.

To pin down Cutler, Greene needed to link his punches into combinations. However he was throwing single shots, albeit hard ones, while Cutler outmanoeuvred him.

Greene found his urgency in the 10th and last round, but Cutler withstood the assault, tying up Greene when he had to to win a unanimous decision, 98-92 and 97-93 twice.

Kayla Allen , the first female fighter signed by Zuffa Boxing, was too much for Hungarian veteran Edina Kiss.

Allen kept her shape, gloves high, as she moved well on her feet. Soon she was bombarding Kiss.

A clean cross landed in a combination, knocking Kiss back a few paces. Gamely Kiss tried to club punches back at her at the start of the second round but Allen asserted herself, the right smacking into the Hungarian's chin and she brought through a hard left as well. With Kiss turning away, Allen shook Kiss up. The Hungarian stumbled into the ropes and the referee issued a count.

Allen meted out punishment in the third round, lining up straight one-twos and Kiss retired on her stool at the break.

Alex MacMillan delivered another stunning finish in his second consecutive fight. From the opening bell he stormed after fellow unbeaten prospect Guillaume Azagier, cutting off the ring. He feinted at the body but struck mercilessly to the head. A huge right over the top dropped Azagier heavily in the first round.

MacMillan didn't need a further invitation. He stayed on him and smashed him back to the canvas before the end of the session.

In the second round, he rapidly had Azagier reeling and as the towel sailed in from the corner, MacMillan put him down a third time to end the fight.

Mexican Olympian Rogelio Romero maintained his 100 per cent knockout ratio in his seven-fight pro career as he handed a first defeat to Moldovan puncher Aurel Ignat.

The heavy-handed Romero hammered Ignat with southpaw left hooks. He hurt the Moldovan, but Ignat returned fire.

In the third round Romero forgot his mouthpiece and started taking hits.

Troubled by Ignat's fightback, Romero solved his problems with a hellacious right hook that left Ignat wobbling and saw the referee stop him on his feet.

Fred Pullen , a national amateur champion for West Ham, made his professional debut, handling Italy's Leonardo Faretina over four rounds.

The London southpaw's lead right fired in at the start of the second round to drop Faretina. But the Italian rose quickly and proved obdurate for the rest of the contest. Pullen controlled the bout with his sharp-shooting, winning 40-35.

In a well-matched eight-rounder top American prospect Alexis De La Cerda and Ireland's Cain Lewis put their unbeaten records on the line.

De Le Cerda ramped up the pressure and by the sixth the mobile Lewis was cut and bleeding. The Irishman dug in and drove De Le Cerda back in the last round, but the American won a unanimous decision, 80-72, 79-73 and 79-74 for the judges.

Cesar Mateo Tapia came out strongly against Leo Ruiz but couldn't sustain it as the latter took over their 10-rounder, finishing well to win unanimously, 97-93 and 96-94 twice.

articles.title: Jake Paul, MVP sued by boxer Heather Hardy for $10 million lawsuit over alleged 'career-ending' fight
articles.summary: In a 54-page complaint, the ex-champ alleges foul play regarding a "career-ending" fight with Paul's MVP that resulted in "permanent brain injury" to the 44-...
articles.body:
Former WBO featherweight champion Heather Hardy has filed a lawsuit seeking more than $10 million from Most Valuable Promotions, its co-founder Jake Paul, its COO Bryce Holden, and Holden Boxing.

The complaint stems from a fight between Hardy and seven-division champion Amanda Serrano, an undercard bout for Paul's boxing match against former UFC star Nate Diaz on Aug. 5, 2023. Holden, who became MVP's COO in February 2024, was the licensed promoter for the Paul vs. Diaz event through Holden Boxing.

Hardy alleges that the defendants exploited Hardy's reputation and financial vulnerability to organize a "dangerous and unnecessary rematch" with Serrano.

"Defendants knew, or should have known, that the bout presented an extraordinary and foreseeable risk of serious neurological harm to Hardy."

The 54-page complaint, filed Sept. 23 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, Dallas Division, alleges that the fight with Serrano was "career-ending" for Hardy and resulted in "permanent brain injury" to the 44-year-old.

Serrano and Hardy fought for the first time in 2019. On that occasion, Serrano defeated Hardy decisively to defend her unified featherweight titles. Hardy underwent three fights afterward, suffering another defeat to Jessica Camara before winning two low-key bouts in October 2022 and February 2023.

The complaint portrays Hardy as approaching the end of her career after suffering years of accumulated punishment when the Serrano rematch was made for August 2023. It alleges that Hardy's longtime promoter, Lou DiBella, refused to help arrange the rematch because he considered it unsafe.

Serrano vs. Hardy 2 was also allegedly opposed by promoter Larry Goldberg, Hardy's trainers, and her friends, including Gleason's Gym founder Bruce Silverglade.

MVP, however, is alleged in the complaint to have bypassed DiBella and "exploited" Hardy's desperate financial position to secure the fight anyway.

The complaint acknowledges that Holden Boxing was the licensed promoter for the fight, not MVP, but argues that Holden served as a "liability shield" so MVP could "enjoy the financial benefits of promotion without formally assuming the regulatory responsibilities of the licensed promoter."

Serrano landed 242 power punches on Hardy during their 20-minute bout in August 2023, according to boxing stat-tracker CompuBox.

The complaint alleges that the fight ended Hardy's career and caused her permanent neurological damage.

The damage became more apparent, Hardy claims, in early 2024 when she was preparing for a bare-knuckle fight and lost vision during light sparring. Hardy says she was told by an ophthalmologist that the problem originated in her brain, leading her to retire.

"Dr. Curreri concluded that Ms. Hardy now suffers from a permanent disability marked by traumatic brain injury, memory loss, double vision, anxiety disorder, spatial confusion, and perception and depth inaccuracies, among other impairments. "According to Dr. Curreri, these symptoms left Ms. Hardy unable to concentrate and, in all likelihood, incapable of maintaining regular employment. Dr. Curreri's assessment connected Hardy's injury to the rematch itself."

"According to Dr. Curreri, these symptoms left Ms. Hardy unable to concentrate and, in all likelihood, incapable of maintaining regular employment. Dr. Curreri's assessment connected Hardy's injury to the rematch itself."

Hardy said she now relies on Medicaid and prescription medication to cope on a day-to-day basis. She claimed she can only coach for a few hours before the symptoms force her to stop.

Hardy brings five causes of action against the defendants: gross negligence, negligent undertaking, negligence per se, ordinary negligence and violation of the Muhammad Ali Boxing Reform Act.

She alleges that the defendants violated Texas boxing regulations and federal law by concealing who controlled the promotion, improperly using Holden Boxing as the licensed promoter and depriving her of independent, conflict-free representation.

In addition to more than $10 million in damages, Hardy is seeking legal costs and an injunction requiring the defendants to take measures to prevent similar harm to other fighters in the future.

The claim argues that Hardy's case was not a one-off incident but rather part of a consistent pattern that represented the "Defendants' lack of care and concern for fighter safety" and how they placed "commercial interests ahead of fighter safety." Two other examples detailed in the suit are those of Isis Sio and Shadasia Green.

Sio fought the MVP-promoted Jocelyn Camarillo on a ProBoxTV card in March 2026. Camarillo knocked Sio unconscious in the first round of their obvious mismatch. Sio left the ring on a stretcher and entered a medically induced coma.

In April 2026, Shadasia Green was left hospitalized after suffering a brain bleed in her fight with Lani Daniels. Per the complaint:

"Green complained of head pain in the fourth round and cried out for help, yet the fight continued until the ninth round before officials stopped it."

Hardy's complaint also accuses MVP of "forum shopping and rule bending.".

The former champion claims that MVP identified a commercially valuable matchup and that, if it presented regulatory or safety concerns, would place it in a jurisdiction with less stringent oversight where an otherwise unsafe fight may be allowed to proceed. Hardy listed two Paul fights as examples in her suit: Paul vs. Mike Tyson in November 2024 and the canceled Paul vs. Gervonta "Tank" Davis exhibition in November 2025.

Although Serrano vs. Hardy 2 took place more than three years before the lawsuit was filed, Hardy argues that her claims remain timely because she did not discover the defendants' allegedly concealed role in arranging the fight until her attorneys investigated the matter in March 2026.

articles.title: AEW All Out 2026 Winners, Live Grades, Reaction and Highlights
articles.summary: In a sold-out Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois on September 26, All Elite Wrestling presented the fifth edition of All Out.
articles.body:
In a sold-out Now Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois on September 26, All Elite Wrestling presented the fifth edition of All Out.

Will Ospreay looked to finally defeat Jon Moxley to defend his AEW Men's World Championship. Cage and Cope, Young Bucks and FTR collided in a Ladder match for the Men's World Tag Team Championships.

The Brawling Birds and Divine Dominion collided in a Chicago Street Fight for the Women's World Tag Team Championships. Willow Nightingale and Thekla collided for a chance to fight Mercedes Moné at WrestleDream.

This was just the beginning of a show that promised to deliver massive spectacle. Check out all the winners, grades and highlights from All Out below.

Tailgate Brawl: "Jungle" Jack Perry vs. Katsuyori Shibata

Last Time in Action: "Jungle" Jack Perry lost in the Casino Gauntlet, and Katsuyori Shibata alongside Hook, Anthony Bowens and Action Andretti lost to Lio Rush and The Rascalz (All In, August 30).

Perry tested Shibata early by challenging his technical chops and strikes until a chop from The Wrestler sent him tumbling out of the ring, which sent the match into a commercial break.

Back from break, Jungle Jack caught Shibata on the apron with a boot, only to again fall to the chops of The Wrestler followed by a Snap Suplex on the apron.

Perry countered a second Suplex attempt into one of his own. Jungle Jack caught a PK and turned into the Snare Trap. Shibata kicked his way free but ran into a Tiger Driver for a near-fall.

Perry went for the Running Knee, but Shibata chopped him down hard then repeatedly chopped Jungle Jack in the corner.

Perry caught Shibata in a grapple and shifted into a pin for the surprise three count. After the win, Jungle Jack immediately found a camera to question where Samoa Joe is before yelling for him to arrive.

Hook, Bowens and Andretti arrived to reveal the returning Samoan Submission Machine, who marched to the ring.

Perry demanded a handshake and instead got a Headbutt courtesy of The Samoan Submission Machine.

This was a fun match that did its job well enough though will likely be forgotten by the end of the pay-per-view.

What matters more is that Joe is back, and he is ready to fight again. Perry vs. Joe should be a much more substantial bout and a major test for Jungle Jack.

He survived Shibata with a trick pin. It still does not feel like he is ready to beat Joe, but that may be the point.

He is looking to learn from Joe destroying him rather than expecting to beat the former two-time AEW men's world champion.

Taz questioned the intelligence of Perry going after world champions and exchanged strikes with Shibata, selling the test Jungle Jack was putting himself through.

The chest of Perry was left pure red by the end.

The crowd was behind Jungle Jack throughout until Joe arrived. The threat of Joe "killing" Perry had the crowd excited.

Tailgate Brawl: Sisters of Sin vs. Mina Shirakawa and Queen Aminata

Last Time in Action: Queen Aminatana and Mina Shirakawa defeated Emily Jaye and Georgia South (Collision, September 19); Skye Blue and Julia Hart lost to Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron (All Out: Buy In, August 30).

This match started back-and-forth and physical as The Sisters of Sin tried to slow down Mina and Aminata, but she kept her pace even past the commercial break.

Mina caught Blue with a Figure-Four into a Double Foot Stomp from Aminata, but Hart caught Aminata with a Superkick.

The Sisters of Sin both locked in Octopus Stretches on their opponents, who reversed out. Aminata went for Off with Her Head but got caught by Hart.

Blue twice almost rolled up Mina. The second was aided by a strike to Mina by Hart. While Mina kicked out, she was dazed, setting up a Code Blue to win.

This got sloppy in moments, but the women recovered quickly to keep the action moving, leading to an overall solid contest.

This was only on the Tailgate Brawl to make sure Blue got a spotlight in Chicago, but AEW did enough to sell the reason for this match over recent Collisions.

Maybe the win is enough to propel The Sisters of Sin into Women's World Tag Team Championships contention again.

Hart and Blue are the best established team in AEW and should eventually get a run with the gold. Taking down a formerly undefeated team should help them get there.

Hopefully this won't end up putting Mina and Aminata back on ROH exclusively. This women's division needs a variety of fresh stars at the top to keep things exciting.

Blue and Hart def. Mina and Aminata by pinfall.

The hometown woman, Blue, got the biggest chants of anyone in this match.

Beyond a couple shortcuts, it felt like The Sisters of Sin were mostly playing face in this, especially Blue, who fed off the crowd energy.

The Artist of Stardom Championships continue to be referenced on AEW TV, but it is a shame that The Triangle of Madness running the gold has not led to more Stardom star appearances.

Tailgate Brawl - No DQ: The Dogs and Death Riders vs. The Bang Bang Gang

Last Time in Action: Daniel Garcia lost to Andrade El Ídolo, and Wheeler Yuta lost to "Speedball" Mike Bailey (Collision, September 19). David Finlay and Clark Connors alongside Gabe Kidd and Pac defeated Ace Austin, Austin Gunn and Colten Gunn alongside Juice Robinson, and "Switchblade" Jay White defeated Adam Priest (Collision, September 12).

This was immediately chaos from the bell as it was clarified this was going to be No DQ, No Count Out and all NFL references.

Football charges and tackles became the frequent focus of the action, trying to isolate and beat down singular members of the opposition.

Ace rallied The Bang Bang Gang by running around and past all four heels to get the football to the end zone (ring).

Marina Shafir and Juice got into it after Marina broke up a pin. The Problem responded with a Judo Throw into a Headlock, rolling both to the outside.

Finlay caught Austin with a helmet for a near-fall. The Bang Bang Gang rallied back, and Switchblade sealed the win with a Switchblade to Yuta.

This was an absolute blast and the clear standout of the Tailgate Brawl. Everyone was having a blast from the wrestlers to the fans.

AEW has always been good at big team brawls like this, but this was completely different than a Stadium Stampede or Anarchy in the Arena courtesy of a heavy focus on the NFL references.

Ace got the best spot of the match and looked like a star despite coming in as the least established act of the contest.

White got a nice pin at the end to sell that he is still a big problem for any heel on this roster, though it does not feel like he is done yet with The Dogs.

The second Switchblade vs. Finlay match is the final payoff and needs a big stage. It could be WrestleDream.

White, Ace, Austin and Colten def. Yuta, Garcia, Connors and Finlay by pinfall.

Before the match, Mick Foley got the inside scoop backstage on The Bang Bang Gang's strategy.

Connors came out with a beer keg while The Death Riders brought football pads.

The Dogs and Death Riders also got NFL introductions during their entrance.

The crowd had fun with the NFL references, even getting in a "Green Bay sucks" chant.

Juice and Marina played coaches at ringside for much of this with straight faces.

The talent ran down to seconds on the clock before the victory, leading to a quick transition to the PPV.

National Championship: Andrade El Ídolo (c) vs. Pac

Last Time in Action: Pac defeated Ace Austin (Collision, September 23). Andrade El Ídolo successfully defended the National Championship against Daniel Garcia (Collision, September 19).

These two started slow, but El Ídolo ran into a strong German Suplex from Pac. Andrade responded with Three Amigos, only for The Bastard to fight to the floor before the third.

Pac ducked a diving Andrade then distracted referee Aubrey Edwards to allow Marina Shafir to gouge the eyes of El Ídolo.

The Bastard took over the action until Andrade tossed Marina into the crowd. El Ídolo almost caught Pac back in the ring with a Fake-Out Standing Moonsault.

Pac continued to get in the way of El Ídolo taking off his pants to the annoyance of the crowd. Andrade successfully hit the Three Amigos and knocked Pac out of the ring.

Finally, El Ídolo got his pants off followed by a Torneo to Pac on the floor. When Andrade tried to get in his typical crowd selfie, Marina choked out the woman.

Pac used the distraction to knock Andrade back into the ring followed by a Springboard 450 Splash for the near-fall.

Andrade landed on his feet out of a Top-Rope Headscissors and landed Día de los Muertos, only for Pac to roll outside. The Bastard Suplexed El Ídolo into the barricade for a near-count-out.

Pac then set up for the Black Arrow. Andrade ducked it and set up a DM, only for Marina to get on the apron and charm El Ídolo.

Pac took advantage with a Rebound Clothesline into the Brutalizer. Andrade shifted the leverage into a pin for the stolen victory.

This was a great opener that highlighted the long-known truth that these two are a perfect pair in the ring.

The long run-time in this contest was never obvious because they kept things fresh and engaging.

From playing on all of Andrade's established character flaws to showcasing more than ever how good Marina is as a manager, this match flew by without relying on big drama.

The final stretch sold that either man could win, and Pac looked like he had the win while Andrade escape The Death Riders' best tricks for now.

It seems like Andrade will need to lose the National Championship before he goes after the AEW Men's World Championship, so his title reign is unlikely to last much longer.

It has still been a major success so far, and Andrade is one of the most popular stars in AEW.

Andrade def. Pac by pinfall to retain the National Championship.

Before the match, Renee Paquette explained that Pac saw himself as the more prepared athlete between himself and the champion.

"He's our bastard"/"How you know?" dueling chants started this match beautifully.

Andrade lost his focus because of Marina multiple times, which could be his Achilles' heel in the future unless he gets a manager that keep him focused.

articles.title: Fisher vs Pirotton: Johnny Fisher wins by majority decision in first fight for Zuffa Boxing
articles.summary: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher wins his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena.
articles.body:
British heavyweight Johnny Fisher won his first fight under the Zuffa Boxing banner with a majority points victory over a bloodied Michael Pirotton at London's Copper Box Arena.

The 27-year-old Essex fighter was the deserved winner in a close bout, but looked laboured at times and appeared to feel the pace over 10 rounds.

Belgian Pirotton, 30, was hampered by a cut around the eye from early in the fight but battled gamely.

He was rocked in the final round as Fisher briefly threatened a stoppage, but Pirotton held on as the judges scored it 95-95, 98-92 and 96-95.

Fisher left the ring shortly after his arm was raised without doing an interview and also did not attend a post-fight interview.

It was Fisher's 15th victory in 16 professional contests on his first appearance since leaving Matchroom Boxing and joining Dana White's Zuffa promotion.

The 7,500-capacity Copper Box was some way short of full, with the upper tier closed and empty seats dotted around the arena.

But Fisher's "Bosh Army" did their best to fill the gaps with noise, giving the "Romford Bull" a raucous reception.

Alongside his social-media star father "Big John" , Fisher has built a loyal following through an unusually unfiltered glimpse into family life, training camps and the pair's well-documented enthusiasm for Chinese takeaways.

Fisher started with intent, swinging heavy hooks and reddening Pirotton's eye in the opening round.

The little-known Belgian was unfazed by the home support or Fisher's pressure, but his eye was cut by the second.

"I can see, don't stop the fight," Pirotton told the referee before a doctor examined him in the fourth.

Allowed to continue, he came out firing, but Fisher responded with a flurry to head and body.

Blood stained Pirotton's white shorts, yet he rallied in the fifth - his best round - as Fisher began to look tired and static.

Among those in attendance were British fighters Derek Chisora, Conor Benn and Caroline Dubois, alongside WWE stars AJ Styles and LA Knight.

WWE is owned by American sports and entertainment group TKO, which is also behind Zuffa Boxing.

The doctor took another look at Pirotton before the seventh but allowed the bout to continue.

Neither man was offering much by the latter stages until a short right hand from Fisher staggered Pirotton in the 10th.

For a moment, a 13th stoppage victory appeared within reach, but Fisher could not find the finishing burst as Pirotton slipped to his third loss in 15 fights.

The Copper Box Arena has already become a fitting stage for the contrasting fortunes of Fisher's career. In July 2024, he overwhelmed Alen Babic in just 36 seconds, producing his most explosive victory to date.

Ten months later, in the same ring, he was comprehensively stopped in five rounds by Doncaster's Dave Allen .

Keen to put that behind him, Fisher got the victory he needed on Saturday - if not quite the emphatic performance he might have wanted.

Fisher has repeatedly insisted he wants to be known as more than a popular ticket-seller with a catchy nickname and viral antics.

His profile has raced ahead of his achievements in the ring, and the two meetings with Allen offered the clearest indication yet of the gap he must close if his British-title ambitions are to become reality.

Current British heavyweight champion Richard Riakporhe has already offered Fisher a shot at the belt. The former cruiserweight world champion would represent a considerable jump in level and a far sterner examination than Pirotton.

Former world champion Deontay Wilder has also been mooted as an opponent, but a meeting with former world-title challenger Dillian Whyte appears the more realistic possibility, with Fisher saying there is a "good chance" that contest could come next.

articles.title: Viéitez supera a Palmquist en un combate histórico y se convierte en la primera campeona de WOW FC
articles.standfirst: La peleadora española remontó una pelea que tenía practicamente perdida para consagrarse como la monarca de peso paja
articles.summary: La peleadora española remontó una pelea que tenía practicamente perdida para consagrarse como la monarca de peso paja
articles.body: El regreso de WOW FC a Sevilla con WOW 32 ha sido todo un éxito. Casi 5.000 personas han acudido al Polideportivo San Pablo para ver una velada llena de grandes combates, donde la guinda del pastel ha sido la increíble remontada de Sara Viéitez (4-2) ante Hanna Palmquist (3-1) para convertirse en la primera campeona de la historia de la promotora por decisión unánime tras un enfrentamiento que tenía practicamente perdido. Los dos primeros rounds fueron un monólogo de 'Hannimal' que incluso logró un knockdown y tuvo en sus manos el K.O. Sin embargo, gracias a su pundonor y al apoyo del público Sara fue entrando poco a poco en la pelea, se repuso, e impuso su cardio para quitar el invicto al Palmquist. De hecho, en el cuarto round fue Sara la que tuvo el K.O. en sus manos, e incluso Hanna llegó a negar con la cabeza dando la espalda a su rival, pero finalmente aguantó hasta la decisión. Épica es la palabra. Por otro lado, Dani Ladero (5-3) también volvió a la senda del triunfo al dominar a Przemysław Dzwoniarek (4-4) por decisión unánime tras su 'no contest' -sin resultado- ante Enoc Solves en el combate por el cinturón de peso semipesado, mientras que en el evento co estelar Pepe Torres (11-1) consiguió una sufrida victoria por decisión unánime ante un combativo Jefferson Vargas (5-3) que estuvo a punto de finalizarle en el primer asalto. Eso sí, sin duda el otro gran combate de la noche fue el que enfrentó a Jefferson Batista (7-1) y Junior Hernández (6-2-1). El peleador peruano mostró una resistencia inusual al resistir hasta dos knockdowns por parte de Batista, que sacó todo su arsenal para intentar finalizar a 'El Matador'. Sin embargo, se tuvo que conformar con una decisión unánime tras la que ambos salieron ovacionados por el espectáculo que acababan de protagonizar. Como era de esperar, más tarde Arturo Guillén -Presidente de WOW FC- les otorgó el bono a mejor pelea de la velada, junto con la de Sara y Hanna. En los combates profesionales, el debut de Sara Cabeza de Vaca (1-0) fue más que complicado ante Ludmila Scurco (2-2), a la que se acabó imponiendo por decisión unánime. Por otro lado, Charlie Hatton (2-1) consiguió uno de los K.O. de la noche ante Theo Pino (0-2), y Alejandro Manzorro (1-1) fue profeta en su tierra tras finalizar a Nuno Krug (0-1) con ground and pound en el segundo round. Además, Pablo Colado (3-0) hizo vibrar al público sevillano manteniendo su invicto ante Vitor Enrique (3-2) a base de codazos que le aseguraron el bono a mejor K.O. Otro nombre a destacar fue Enrique Kakulov (1-0), que brilló con luz propia ante Christian Berrocal (3-3) tal y como prometió. El campeón de España de kickboxing y boxeo no cumplió con su promesa de finalizar en el primer asalto debido al buen hacer de Berrocal en lucha, pero en el segundo no perdonó para debutar con éxito en amateur en MMA. Su siguiente objetivo es dar el salto a profesional con un objetivo claro: el WOW 34 Valencia en el Roig Arena.

articles.title: Johnny Fisher overcomes Michael Pirotton in heavyweight brawl winning a majority decision after 10-round battle
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher is pushed to his limits by Belgium's Michael Pirotton; Fisher started strongly against Pirotton but had to hold on for majority decision win at the Copper Box Arena in London
articles.body:
Fisher punched forward to take a lead, but as his energy reserves waned he began to look increasingly vulnerable while the Belgian battled back.

The Romford favourite forced himself through to the finish, taking a majority decision win, but it was testing.

Having just watched gym-mate Craig Richards lose in the chief support, Fisher looked to banish any nerves by plunging forward onto the front foot. He went straight for the Belgian with double jabs.

Pirotton hefted a left hook across, but Fisher's "Romford Bull Army" of supporters had found their voice. Feet stamping, voices raised, they chanted Fisher's name to create a raucous atmosphere in the Copper Box.

Fisher responded driving himself into Pirotton, but leaving himself open when he leaned over his front leg.

The Belgian did catch Fisher with his right cross. But the "Romford Bull" also showed off some of his work with new trainer Tony Sims, every now and then bobbing and weaving under an attack to stay in the pocket and pummel Pirotton's body.

Fisher was landing head shots and Pirotton was cut over the left eye early on. It was in a bad position and the doctor had a close look at it in the fourth round.

On resumption, Fisher stormed forward, sensing his moment. He hit Pirotton with a hard left hook to body, and then launched his right down on his head. That combination worked for him and Fisher tenderised the body to open up the head.

He shook up Pirotton and directed him back into the ropes. But getting through the fourth, Pirotton fired back in the fifth round.

Power began to drain away from Fisher's punches and he held his feet. Pirotton blasted his right into a tiring Fisher and caught him with following head shots.

Fisher struck back before the end of the fifth round but he was flagging. In the sixth round, his supporters bellowed him on as Fisher searched for his second wind. He did find chopping hooks that rattled Pirotton round the head.

In the seventh round Fisher's right swung wildly, missing, but he launched himself back in with an explosive left to drive Pirotton into the ropes.

The Belgian, increasingly on the offensive, continued to make it a bruising night's work for Fisher.

He threaded his right over Fisher's jab, a fine shot. Even though he'd picked up a second cut round his left eye, Pirotton was undaunted, looking to chip into Fisher's lead and he managed to stand his ground.

Pirotton's left eye was almost fully closed by the last round. Fisher hurt him, lashing in shots as the crowd roared. He summoned up his final dregs of energy, windmilling rights at Pirotton as he went for him.

Fisher, exhausted at the end of the battle, couldn't find a decisive finish and one judge had the two heavyweights level at 95-95. A second saw it close at 96-95 but the third had Fisher ahead 98-92.

articles.title: Dillian Whyte wants fight against Johnny Fisher: 'I'll be surprised if it goes past three or four rounds'
articles.summary: Johnny Fisher was pushed to his limits by Belgium's Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena in London on Saturday night, with Sky Sports expert Johnny Nelson insisting it would be too risky for him to face the experienced Whyte - who was ringside - in his next outing
articles.body:
The Brixton heavyweight was watching from ringside as Fisher battled to a majority-decision victory over Michael Pirotton at The Copper Box on Saturday night.

Whyte is ready to return following his loss to Moses Itauma last August and has welcomed a verbal challenge from Fisher.

"Johnny Fisher has been calling me out for a while. He wants to fight me. I'm well up for that fight," Whyte told Sky Sports .

"I knock Johnny Fisher out. It's heavyweight boxing, anything can happen. I could get caught high on the head like I did last time out, but I'll knock Johnny Fisher out.

"I'll be surprised if it goes past three or four rounds. I'm an ageing dog but I still have all of my teeth."

Whyte, who holds wins over the likes of Joseph Parker and Alexander Povetkin, insists he would relish an explosive showdown with Fisher, who has 12 knockouts in his 15 victories.

"He's a bit erratic and he's open in lots of areas but he's dangerous," said Whyte. "He's swinging big punches, a big man, and he hits hard so yeah, I think it would be an exciting fight while it lasts."

Asked about Fisher's biggest threat, Whyte added: "Big overhand rights really. That's it really, but I've fought the best of my generation. The reason this fight attracts me is because it's dangerous. My last fight lasted a round so people could be thinking I'm washed up and finished now so let them run with that.

"I don't mind being a stepping stone because you need a stepping stone to step somewhere else. Let's go. They want to fight me. I was at home relaxing, they offered me out, so let's get it on."

Sky Sports expert Johnny Nelson has warned that Whyte could be 'too much' for Fisher.

"No he can't [keep having fights like that]," Nelson told Sky Sports .

"I spoke to Dillian Whyte, who is kind of looking at being a potential opponent for Johnny Fisher.

"I think Dillian knows too much for him, regardless of what stage of his career he's at.

"They need to think smartly, matchmaking him, if they want to get him to a British title attempt.

"I wouldn't put him in with Dillian Whyte, because Dillian knows too much.

"He's strong, he's rugged and he's experienced."

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Tyson Fury puts chances of mammoth all-British heavyweight clash vs Anthony Joshua going ahead at one per cent
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has claimed that there is now a "one per cent" chance of his fight against Anthony Joshua going ahead; Fury has cast further doubt on the all-British heavyweight fight in an interview on his YouTube channel
articles.body:
On Thursday, confirmation finally arrived that Fury and Joshua's all-British heavyweight showdown will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday December 11 following months of protracted negotiations to stage the biggest fight in British boxing history.

Fury, though, cast doubt on the agreement on Saturday by claiming Joshua was trying to pull out of the fight, and has put his own estimate on the chances of the much-anticipated heavyweight bout going ahead.

Asked on his YouTube channel Furocity what percentage he thinks there is of the fight going ahead, Fury responded: "One per cent.

"If you've got a guy that wants to fight, yeah, and you've got a guy that doesn't want to fight, then how are you going to make that fight happen?

"I've had nearly 40 professional fights, yeah, and I've been on top of this game for over a decade, right? How did I manage to fight all these people before you, all these champions, yeah, for all these titles that there is in boxing, but, yeah, every time it comes to fighting [Joshua]... it never happens.

The announcement for the long-awaited Fury-AJ fight stated that Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and Dana White were staging the bout, although Eddie Hearn, who promotes Joshua, has publicly claimed the American promoter cannot be involved.

Speaking after Johnny Fisher's victory at the Copper Box on Saturday , White said: "I'm involved in the fight.

"If Eddie Hearn really cared about this fight, first of all it would have happened a long time ago, number one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself. I've said this a million times... Sell tickets, cut a TV deal and sell the fight."

White though is now uncertain that the fight will even take place.

"That I don't know," he said. "The guy who's supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time. He hasn't done the fight any favours let's put it that way.

"We'll all know more in the next three or four days."

Fury also claimed that he had initially agreed for the fight to take place at Croke Park in Ireland, a venue that has only hosted two boxing matches in its 142-year history.

"In the beginning, I signed the contract to do the fight in Ireland, in Croke Park, because that's where I wanted to do the fight, Croke Park in Ireland. So if I'd have stuck to my contract, this fight wouldn't have happened, would it?

"There's nothing that I haven't agreed to, nothing. I'll even tie concrete blocks to my boots to make this fight happen. There's nothing that I wouldn't do to make this fight happen."

Despite his initial scepticism, Fury ended his interview by conceding that his signed contracts mean the fight may go ahead after all:

"I do think it'll happen. Because from what I'm hearing, they've been paid already. So the fight's got to happen.

"Not unless [Joshua] wants to give the dough back, which I can't see them wanting to do that."
