articles.title: UFC Vegas 121 live results, highlights and play-by-play
articles.summary: UFC Vegas 121 results, highlights, live discussion and instant play-by-play, reactions and analysis.
articles.body:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) is live TODAY (Sat., Sept. 26, 2026) with UFC Vegas 121 , streaming live online via Paramount+ . The event goes down inside the familiar META APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada.

UFC is back in the warehouse for the first time since early August. And META APEX, this week, is host to an interesting Bantamweight fight, the latest The Ultimate Fighter (TUF) Finale bouts and a slew of bouts featuring names only hardcore fans would recognize.

Raul Rosas Jr. vs. Raoni Barcelos pits youth versus experience, with both men looking to stretch win streaks. Rosas Jr. had a dull win over Rob Font in his last contest, while Barcelos is coming off a an upset over Montel Jackson . With the top of Bantamweight solidified right now, with two or three contenders all but locked in, neither Rosas Jr. nor Barcelos will get a big push up the ladder with a win.

It's still worth seeing them fight, though.

The co-main event, after some late week shuffling , is Norma Dumont vs. Ailin Perez . Perez has one of the better winning streaks in women's mixed martial arts (MMA) right now. She'll pit her wrestling against Dumont's striking ( which famously sliced apart Irene Aldana in The Sphere ).

TUF finals include Ilimbek Akylbek Uulu vs. Mehmmedeli Osmanli and Tina Black vs. Melissa Amaya . Luis Hernandez vs. Sedriques Dumas completes the main card, with Hernandez coming off Contender Series in a hurry to replace Micky Gall .

The featured "Prelims" undercard bout is Rinya Nakamura vs. Brady Hiestand . Rodolfo Vieira vs. Robert Bryczek and Rodolfo Bellato vs. Christian Edwards are also on the undercard.

We are back in the APEX tonight and that means a return to our usual broadcast times.

UFC Vegas 121 "Prelims" will begin at 5 p.m. ET .

UFC Vegas 121 main card is scheduled to start at 8 p.m. ET .

All of UFC Vegas 121 airs on Paramount+ , which you can stream here .

The live blog here starts rolling below at 5 p.m. ET . Come in and say hi!

135 lbs.: Raul Rosas Jr. vs. Raoni Barcelos

185 lbs.: Luis Hernandez vs. Sedriques Dumas

135 lbs.: Ilimbek Akylbek Uulu vs. Mehemmedeli Osmanli

115 lbs.: Tina Black def. Melissa Amaya by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:19)

135 lbs.: Brady Hiestand def. Rinya Nakamura by submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:07) — HIGHLIGHTS

185 lbs.: Rodolfo Vieira def. Robert Bryczek by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

205 lbs.: Christian Edwards def. Rodolfo Bellato by TKO (punches), round 3 (1:47) — HIGHLIGHTS

155 lbs.: Elves Brener def. Josiah Harrell by TKO (punches), round (4:14) — HIGHLIGHTS

135 lbs.: Montel Jackson def. Ricky Simon by TKO (punches), round 2 (2:39) — HIGHLIGHTS

135 lbs.: Alatengheili def. John Castaneda by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28)

115 lbs.: Yasmin Jauregui def. Vanessa Demopoulos by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:02) — HIGHLIGHTS

Round 1: Black lands a nice jab early on. Amaya lands a one-two. Lots of sizing each other up in this bout so far, but not a lot of offense thrown. Amaya has a big wind up on her punches. Black just side-steps out the way of a big overhand attempt. Despite missing a lot, Amaya is the one moving forwards. Black lands a calf kick. And then a check hook. Amaya steps in and Black ducks and cracks her right on the chin. She goes down to one knee. She gets up bloodied and looking very hurt. Black chases her and lands a hook. Amaya is running. Black is trying to catch up, but she's not throwing enough. Black gets her on the fence and lands more punches, but then gets hurt with a counter as the buzzer goes.

Round 2: Amaya blitzes forwards, but Black's footwork allows her to step out of range. Black goes forwards with a one-two that sends Amaya back. Black goes down on a slip and Amaya charges to try and make her pay. Black is up quick, though, and they end up clinching on the fence. They trade knees and Black lands a big hook on the break. That wobbled Amaya. Black lands another right hook. Amaya is really wobbling around. Black closes in and lands a combo that sends her down and forces the ref to step in.

Official decision: Tina Black def. Melissa Amaya by TKO (punches), round 2 (3:19)

Brady Hiestand vs. Rinya Nakamura : Nakamura's wrestling didn't stack up to Hiestand's jiu jitsu. Once Hiestand got into dominant positions on the ground he got deep on an anaconda choke and then, moments later, he got the rear naked choke for the win.

Official decision: Brady Hiestand def. Rinya Nakamura by submission (rear naked choke), round 2 (4:07)

Rodolfo Vieira vs. Robert Bryczek: This wasn't fun to watch. Vieira spend the fight either on top of Bryczek of pushing him into the fence. Bryczek did try and make something fun happened, when he had space, but this ended as a smothering decision win for Vieira.

Official decision: Rodolfo Vieira def. Robert Bryczek by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27)

Rodolfo Bellato vs. Christian Edwards: Edwards landed the last shot in a pretty scrappy (or sloppy) brawl. Edwards was consistently landing more volume, but he was getting hurt by Bellato's power. That included when he got dropped in the first round. In the third, though, Edwards came out more aggressively and let fly with a hook that dropped Bellato. He then followed up for the TKO win.

Official decision: Christian Edwards def. Rodolfo Bellato by TKO (punches), round 3 (1:47)

Elves Brener vs. Josiah Harrell: Brener had Harrell confused by his stance switches and was able to tee off on his opponent from range. Harrell shot for takedowns and took big swings, but this was all Brener. He ended up face-planting Harrell with a right hook.

Official decision: Elves Brener def. Josiah Harrell by TKO (punches), round (4:14)

Montel Jackson vs. Ricky Simon: Jackson lived up to his 'Quick' nickname in this bout. His hands were far too fast for Simon. He tagged him often and knocked him down in the first round. in the second round his sniped Simon again and put him away.

Official decision: Montel Jackson def. Ricky Simon by TKO (punches), round 2 (2:39)

John Castaneda vs. Alatengheili: This was a close fight without too much to write home about. Alatengheili did a lot of head hunting, while Castaneda mixed things up more. Castaneda did the better job on the feet, but Alatengheili mounted a late wrestling attack to take the third round. I scored it for Castaneda, but some of those rounds were razor thin.

Official decision: Alatengheili def. John Castaneda by split decision (28-29, 29-28, 29-28)

Yasmin Jauregui vs. Vanessa Demopoulos: Wow, Jauregui just lit up Demopoulos with landed about fifty strikes in sixty seconds to score a brutal TKO. Jauregui had been out for two years, but a performance like that puts her right back into the mix at Strawweight.

Official decision: Yasmin Jauregui def. Vanessa Demopoulos by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:02)

articles.title: Tony Ferguson lands knockout win at Misfits Boxing event
articles.summary: Tony Ferguson wins by knockout at Misfits Boxing event.
articles.body:
The Tony Ferguson hype train is still rolling.

Not even a last-minute opponent change could stop Ferguson from delivering another standout performance during Misfits Boxing's event in Miami. 'El Cucuy' faced off against Mahmoud Sebie in the co-headliner on Saturday night, defending his MFB Middleweight title. The win extends his streak to three straight with the promotion, but the finish has people talking.

In the opening round, Sebie knocked Tony Ferguson down with a left hook, but Ferguson bounced right back to his feet. The bout looked like a normal Misfits-level boxing match until Sebie stood still, allowing Ferguson to land three unanswered punches on him, dropping him to the canvas in bizarre fashion.

Then, early in the second, it looked like Mahmoud Sebie was his normal self. Throwing power punches early, he caught Tony Ferguson again, wobbling him on his feet. Ferguson fought back and avoided further big shots. Then, just seconds later, Sebie backed himself into the corner and allowed Ferguson to unleash unanswered shots on him. The former UFC star emptied the tank, throwing a long combination of strikes and forcing the referee to step in and end the fight.

An incredibly strange clash between the two. However, Tony Ferguson won't be complaining as he comes away with yet another win. How he has managed to rejuvenate his career after eight straight losses to end his UFC tenure should be studied.

Official result: Tony Ferguson def. Mahmoud Sebie via TKO (Unanswered Punches) at 0:42 of Round 2.

articles.title: Henry Cejudo vs. 'Euphoria' Actor Javon Walton Results, Highlights from Misfits Boxing Card
articles.summary: Former UFC flyweight and bantamweight champion Henry Cejudo defeated Javon Walton by split decision in their showdown on Saturday's Misfits Boxing card.
articles.body:
Former UFC flyweight and bantamweight champion Henry Cejudo defeated Javon Walton by split decision in their showdown on Saturday's Misfits Boxing card.

The judges' scorecards had Cejudo as the winner, 39-37, 39-37, 37-39.

Walton was participating in his fifth professional boxing match and is also an actor, previously appearing on shows such as Euphoria and Under The Bridge .

He was energetic throughout the first two rounds of Saturday's fight, but Cejudo responded with increased pressure to begin the third round and ended their clash on a high note to emerge victorious.

Cejudo's performance was particularly impressive considering he was making his professional boxing debut, overcoming Walton's technical ability by hitting him with several overhand and straight right hands.

Cejudo said in his post-fight interview that he felt the first round didn't go his way, but was still able to make the appropriate adjustments to secure the win (h/t Matthew Wells of MMA Junkie).

While Walton suffered his first professional loss, his overall showing was still admirable after taking the fight on short notice.

He stepped in as Cejudo's opponent on Sept. 15, replacing influencer Nurideen Shabazz after he was forced to withdraw due to injury.

After Cejudo compiled a 16-6-0 record during his professional MMA career, he's now 1-0-0 as a boxer.

articles.title: Sting's Son Steven Borden Injured in Scary Fall with Kevin Knight at AEW All Out
articles.summary: AEW wrestler Steven Borden suffered a legitimate injury during a No. 1 Contender tag team match between him and Darby Allin vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight on Saturday night at All Out.
articles.body:
AEW wrestler Steven Borden suffered a legitimate injury during a No. 1 Contender tag team match between him and Darby Allin vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight on Saturday night at All Out.

Thankfully, AEW play-by-play announcer and senior producer Tony Schiavone provided a positive update on Borden's health later in the evening.

During the match, Borden—the son of wrestling legend Sting—and Knight jumped at each other from the two turnbuckles nearest the ramp. Following the ensuing collision, Borden appeared to be knocked out. The referee checked on Borden before an AEW official slid into the ring. The ref then stopped the match.

Borden is enjoying a quick rise up the professional wrestling ranks. He began training under Allin in May 2024 and started wrestling dark matches for AEW and Ring of Honor in Dec. 2025. Borden made his official wrestling debut on television in August.

articles.title: Brawling Birds Beat Divine Dominion to Retain AEW Tag Titles in a Chicago Street Fight at All Out
articles.summary: The Brawling Birds beat Divine Dominion in a Chicago Street Fight at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships.
articles.body:
The Brawling Birds beat Divine Dominion in a Chicago Street Fight at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships.

This was a brutal match, to say the least.

In the end, the Brawling Birds won by hitting the Two Birds One Stone on Lena Kross onto thumbtacks.

Over the course of their record 168-day title reign, Divine Dominion established themselves as the most dominant women's tag team in AEW history.

After beating Willow Nightingale and Harley Cameron for the titles, Megan Bayne and Lena Kross ran through challengers such as Kris Statlander and Hikaru Shida, Anna Jay and Tay Melo, and Julia Hart and Skye Blue.

Divine Dominion appeared to be unbeatable, but that was until Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor stepped up and emerged as the top contenders.

On the Aug. 5 Grand Slam episode of Dynamite in Mexico, the Brawling Birds teamed with Willow to defeat Divine Dominion and Mercedes Moné in a six-woman tag team match.

That set the stage for Divine Dominion to put the tag team titles on the line against the Brawling Birds at All In.

Since All In was held at Wembley Stadium in London, Hayter and Windsor had a huge advantage in terms of crowd support, as both of them are from England.

The Brawling Birds utilized that edge to the fullest, as they finally toppled Divine Dominion to All In to become the new AEW women's world tag team champions.

However, given Divine Dominion's impressive reign and the fact that they had to compete in enemy territory at All In, they were given a rematch at All Out, but this time with a street fight stipulation.

Despite the type of damage Bayne and Kross were capable of doing in a match with no rules, Hayter and Windsor prevailed at All Out in their first pay-per-view title defense.

articles.title: New Level & Swerve Strickland Beat Hangman Page & Brodido to Retain AEW Trios Titles at All Out 2026
articles.summary: The New Level and Swerve Strickland beat "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido in a six-man tag team match at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW World Trios Championships.
articles.body:
The New Level and Swerve Strickland beat "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido in a six-man tag team match at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW World Trios Championships.

Strickland hit Big Pressure on Bandido for the pin and win after getting out of the 21 Plex.

There were some great moments in this match, including Bandido hitting The New Level and Swerve Strickland with one suplex.

One month ago at All In, Kofi and Austin Creed made their AEW debuts in the Trios Roulette Royale as the surprise partners of Swerve, and they won championship gold in their first match with the company.

Page, Brody King and Bandido entered All In as the trios champs, but they were unable to overcome the energy brought by New Level in their first-ever AEW appearance.

In the weeks that followed All In, New Level and Strickland were fighting champions who defended the titles multiple times on Dynamite.

They were victorious against The Rascalz and against Kyle O'Reilly, Roderick Strong and Orange Cassidy of The Conglomeration before a high-profile defense against The Demand on the go-home episode of Dynamite before All Out.

Given that Page and Brodido were positioned for a rematch, New Level and Strickland vs. The Demand became a de facto play-in match to be part of the All Out card.

Ricochet, Bishop Kaun and Toa Liona gave New Level and Swerve what had been the most difficult test of their young title reign to date, but they were unable to pry away the AEW World Trios Championships.

After Kofi, Creed and Swerve retained, they were confronted by Hangman and Brodido, and given some food for thought from Hangman specifically.

Given his lengthy history with Strickland, Page offered a warning of sorts to New Level, suggesting that Swerve could turn on them at any time, much like he did to others in the past.

Kofi and Creed were unmoved by Page's speech, though, and they turned it around on him by noting that he wasn't necessarily trustworthy in his own right.

At All Out, New Level and Strickland continued to be on the same page, as they took down Page and Brodido in what was their first successful pay-per-view title defense.

articles.title: Young Bucks Beat Cage & Cope, FTR to Win AEW Tag Titles in a Ladder Match at All Out
articles.summary: The Young Bucks beat Adam Copeland and Christian Cage, and FTR to win the AEW World Tag Team Championships in a three-way ladder match at All Out on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Young Bucks beat Adam Copeland and Christian Cage, and FTR to win the AEW World Tag Team Championships in a three-way ladder match at All Out on Saturday.

The Young Bucks won after hitting Cage with a BTE Trigger from the top of the ladder, allowing them to make history.

This was a tough and physical match to say the least. In the end, the Young Bucks endured the brutality and won.

At All In last month, Cage and Cope put the tag team titles on the line against The Young Bucks. While they were victorious and retained the championships, it quickly became apparent that Cage and Cope were marked men.

Following their victory, several of AEW's top tag teams made their way to the ring to confront Cope and Cage, including a returning FTR, The Motor City Machine Guns and The New Level.

With The Young Bucks remaining in the ring as well, five of AEW's top teams were in the squared circle together, thus making it clear that the competition level in the AEW tag team division had reached new heights.

Coming out of All In, The Young Bucks expressed unhappiness over the way their match against Cage and Cope played out, as Christian used a wrench to get the win.

However, when The Bucks called out Cage and Cope, FTR stepped up to them instead, signaling the renewal of a rivalry that has played out for much of AEW's existence.

While The Young Bucks and FTR argued, Cage and Cope made their entrance and challenged both teams to face them in a three-way ladder match at All Out.

Copeland made mention of tables and chairs in addition to ladders, which suggested AEW was trying to do their own version of a TLC match.

Cage and Cope helped create and popularize that match type in WWE in the early 2000s along with two other legendary tag teams in The Hardy Boyz and The Dudley Boyz.

Experience with that stipulation was on the side of Cage and Cope at All Out, but The Young Bucks managed to come out on top and set a new record as four-time AEW world tag team champs.

articles.title: Will Ospreay Beats Jon Moxley to Retain AEW Title at All Out After Historic Win vs. Kenny Omega
articles.summary: Will Ospreay defeated Jon Moxley at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
Will Ospreay defeated Jon Moxley at All Out on Saturday to retain the AEW World Championship.

Ospreay won after hitting Moxley with the Hidden Blade.

This match featured interference from the Death Riders when Ospreay had the upper hand and the referee was temporarily knocked out.

However, Ospready had his own reinforcements, including help from Francesco Akira, "Speedball" Mike Bailey and Andrade El Ídolo.

Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter got involved to counter Marina's efforts.

Later in the match, Ospreay found himself on the wrong end of briefcase attacks.

Moxley soon locked in the Bulldog Choke. However, Ospreay bit his way out of it and turned the tide. He hit a Hidden Blade and Storm Breaker for a near-fall before another Hidden Blade did the job.

Saturday marked Ospreay's first pay-per-view title defense since beating Kenny Omega in the main event of All In last month.

Wrestling in his hometown of London at Wembley Stadium, Ospreay put on a match of the year contender with Omega and won AEW's top prize for the first time in the process.

Leading up to his All In match against Omega, Ospreay was heavily influenced by Moxley, as Ospreay had agreed to train with Mox and The Death Riders in an effort to develop a killer instinct.

Ospreay had been rivals with Moxley and The Death Riders, as they put him out of commission with a neck injury after attacking him last year at Forbidden Door.

Despite that, Ospreay and Moxley formed a bond, and Mox's guidance helped Ospreay win the Owen Hart Cup and secure an AEW world title opportunity at All In.

Ospreay had a falling out with The Death Riders at Redemption when he refused to attack Omega following Omega's successful title defense against Kevin Knight, but the bad blood didn't last for long.

Before Ospreay made his entrance at All In, Mox emerged and handed him a flag, while also giving a nod of approval regarding Ospreay's pursuit of the AEW World Championship.

Coming out of All In, Ospreay was firmly in the crosshairs of numerous wrestlers who wanted a shot at the world title, but based on his résumé and his history with Ospreay, Moxley was the first one to be given an opportunity.

Ospreay got his title reign off to an ideal start at All In by beating the most decorated performer in AEW history, and denying Moxley's attempt to extend his record by becoming a five-time AEW world champ.

articles.title: Final agridulce en la UFC: Barcelos sale en camilla y Rosas Jr. se acerca al récord de Jon Jones
articles.standfirst: El veterano peleador brasileño sufrió una preocupante lesión y el joven de 21 años está cada vez más cerca de ser el campeón más joven de la historia de la promotora
articles.summary: El veterano peleador brasileño sufrió una preocupante lesión y el joven de 21 años está cada vez más cerca de ser el campeón más joven de la historia de la promotora
articles.body: La Fight Night celebrada está madrugada en el META Apex de Las Vegas ha cumplido con la Ley de Murphy de la UFC. Cuanto menos mediático es el evento, más sorprende a los fanáticos del deporte. El colofón lo pusieron Raúl Rosas Jr. (13-1) y Raoni Barcelos (22-6) en el peso gallo, donde finalmente fue el peleador mexicano el que extendió su racha a seis victorias consecutivas tras una preocupante lesión del brasileño en el quinto asalto después de un gran combate, lo que le acerca a la oportunidad titular con apenas 21 años y al sueño de ser el campeón más joven de la historia de la UFC. Eso sí, todo paso a un segundo plano teniendo en cuenta que el veterano de peso gallo tuvo que salir en camilla. El primer asalto fue toda una declaración de intenciones de 'El Niño Problema', que a base de golpes rectos logró cerrar el ojo izquierdo de un Barcelos que no rehuyó del intercambio. De hecho, fue Raoni el que se impuso en el segundo asalto gracias a su volumen de golpeo, e incluso la esquina de Rosas Jr. le pedía más tranquilidad para no quedarse sin cardio. El tercero volvió a ser una guerra de golpes, scrambles y pequeños detalles que colocaron a Barcelos con ventaja, y en el cuarto el peleador brasileño puso pie y medio en la victoria. Sin embargo, Raúl aprovechó su juventud para meter presión en el round definitivo, y en un intento de derribo ocurrió lo impensable, ya que el combate se tuvo que parar por una lesión de Barcelos que todavía tiene que confirmarse. Un final agridulce teniendo en cuenta que había sido una de las peleas del año. En el combate co estelar, Norma Dumont (13-4) y Ailín Pérez (14-2) colisionaron en un duelo con un beef muy personal que empeoró con el careo del viernes, donde la brasileña lanzó billetes y preservativos a la argentina. El combate dejó mucho que desear teniendo en cuenta las expectativas, y para más inri 'Fiona' se llevó la victoria con una polémica decisión unánime después de que ambas casi llegasen a las manos de nuevo una vez se acabaron los tres asaltos. Uno de los combates que más expectación había generado durante la semana era el de Luis Hernández (9-0) contra Sedrique Dumas (10-6, 1NC). Luis, que también trabaja como policía en Miami, aceptó en corto aviso un enfrentamiento ante un peleador con un total de 15 arrestos. Apenas 11 días después de ganarse un contrato con la UFC en las Dana White's Contender Series, Hernández sometió a Dumas en menos de un minuto para debutar por todo lo alto. Ojito con él porque dará mucho que hablar en peso medio. En la cartelera estelar también se disputaron las dos finales del mítico de The Ultimate Fighter en peso paja femenino y peso gallo. En el peso paja femenino fue Tina Black (17-4, 1NC) la que noqueó a Melissa Amaya (9-1) después de una guerra sin cuartel en la que impuso su poder para sobrevivir a una montaña rusa de emociones. En el peso gallo el final fue mucho más triste e inesperado, ya que un rodillazo ilegal de Mahammadali Osmanli (13-2) ante Ilimbek Akylbek (12-3) acabó en una descalificación que traerá mucha polémica. En la cartelera preliminar hubo varias actuaciones destacadas. En el primer combate del evento, Yazmin Jauregui (12-2) consiguió noquear a Vanessa Demopoulos (11-9) en menos de un minuto después de un aluvión de golpes. Otro nombre a tener en cuenta es el de Montel Jackson (16-4) en el peso gallo, ya que finalizó a un hueso duro como Ricky Simón (22-8-1) después de dos increíbles combinaciones de rectos de manera consecutiva. El momento más emotivo lo protagonizó Elves Brener (17-6), antiguo rival de Joel Álvarez, ya que noqueó con un gran croché de derechas a Josiah Harrell (11-2) y se lo dedicó a Allan Nascimento, que falleció recientemente de manera repentina y era uno de los pilares del gimnasio Chute Box. Además, Christian Edwards (9-5) protagonizó la remontada de la cartelera tras noquear a Rodolfo Bellato (13-4-1, 1NC) en el tercer asalto después de aguantar un knockdown y estar al borde de la derrota.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: Dana White casts doubt on fight after 24 hours of chaos
articles.summary: There is fresh uncertainty around the proposed Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight - after Dana White said he did not know whether it would happen.
articles.body:
Two days after the announcement British boxing had waited a decade for, Dana White - the UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief named as one of the figures promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua - was asked whether the fight would actually happen.

White was speaking at London's Copper Box on Saturday, where British heavyweight Johnny Fisher beat Michael Pirotton on his Zuffa Boxing debut. But for much of the media in attendance another heavyweight fight dominated the evening.

Asked whether Wednesday's scheduled Fury-Joshua news conference in London would take place, White added: "I have no idea."

On Thursday, Fury and Joshua were officially announced to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, live globally on Netflix. By Friday, that certainty had unravelled.

A dispute over who is entitled to promote the event led to claims of contractual breaches, talk of possible replacement fights and another flurry of cryptic social-media posts.

Even by boxing's recent standards, the past 24 hours have been extraordinary - and not a particularly flattering look for the sport.

Why has White's involvement caused a problem?

Netflix and Saudi powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's fight announcement was striking for who it included - and who it did not. The event was presented as a collaboration involving Alalshikh's The Ring and White.

There was no mention of Matchroom's Eddie Hearn, who has promoted Joshua throughout his professional career, or Queensberry's Frank Warren, Fury's long-time promoter.

White's involvement was not entirely unexpected.

The Zuffa Boxing promoter has been saying for weeks he would be involved in Fury-Joshua.

Hearn has been equally adamant he would not. After Thursday's announcement, Hearn said Joshua's contract specifically prevented White and American sports entertainment company TKO from having a promotional role, claiming Netflix had not been made aware of that provision.

Hearn said there had been breaches of the agreement which needed to be resolved and cast doubt on whether Wednesday's news conference would go ahead.

Fury says a similar restriction originally appeared in his own contract but was removed because he wanted White involved.

Warren has taken a more pragmatic position. Speaking to BBC Sport before the latest dispute escalated, he said his understanding was White had helped secure the Netflix deal and compromises had been necessary to get the fight made.

On Saturday, White was generally non-committal on the future of the contest but much clearer in his criticism of Hearn. "The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight," White said. "He hasn't done the fight any favours."

How did it go from 'official' to rumours it could be off?

The uncertainty intensified on Friday evening.

Reports emerged that Fury-Joshua could be in jeopardy and alternative fights for 11 December were being discussed, including Ryan Garcia against the recently retired three-weight undisputed champion Terence Crawford.

Crawford appeared as surprised as anyone, publicly questioning the suggestion he could be fighting Garcia.

In a video posted on social media, he claimed Joshua and Hearn were "trying to pull out" and blamed the dispute largely on Hearn's objection to White.

There has been no announcement from Joshua saying he intends to withdraw.

On Instagram, Alalshikh posted pictures of himself with White and later shared a cryptic message in Arabic about somebody attempting to "stab you where you told them it hurts", although he made no explicit reference to Fury-Joshua.

Hearn, meanwhile, posted a picture with a shushing emoji and the message: "Bet against me."

For a fight negotiated so publicly for so many years, the familiar mix of claims, counter-claims and cryptic posts had returned almost immediately.

Among the media in east London on Saturday, much of the conversation centred around Fury-Joshua.

Who had heard what? Was the fight genuinely in danger? Would Wednesday's news conference happen? And, with White in the building, would he provide any clarity afterwards?

Instead, his post-fight comments only underlined the uncertainty.

White has been openly critical of Hearn, while the precise nature of his own role in Fury-Joshua remains at the heart of the dispute. That distinction could prove significant when lawyers examine exactly what Joshua's contract permits.

During Saturday's US broadcast of the Zuffa Boxing card, it was suggested White was helping Alalshikh on a personal level rather than acting as a promoter. White rejected that interpretation. "I don't know where that came from," he said. "That was weird."

And White offered another tease when asked whether he would attend Wednesday's news conference if it does go ahead. "I guess I'll leave that as a surprise," he said.

As of Saturday night, Netflix continued to list Fury against Joshua at the Principality Stadium on 11 December and said the fighters would attend Wednesday's news conference.

But the contractual disagreement remains unresolved.

The unusual position is that, little more than 48 hours after the fight was officially announced, one of the central figures in its promotion cannot say whether it will happen - or whether its first major launch event will go ahead.

There is too much money, time and work invested in Fury-Joshua for anyone involved to walk away lightly.

But if the past decade has taught boxing anything, an agreement does not necessarily mean the fight is safe. Fury-Joshua is once again waiting for another hurdle to be cleared.

articles.title: UFC Vegas 121: Raoni Barcelos stretchered out, hospitalized after scary fifth-round KO by Raul Rosas Jr.
articles.summary: Barcelos appeared to lose consciousness post-fight and has been transported to the hospital. His condition remains uncertain.
articles.body:
Raul Rosas Jr. emerged from UFC Vegas 121 with the biggest win of his career. We're still not quite sure what happened.

The 21-year-old rising star defeated Raoni Barcelos in his first career main event, getting a needed knockout in the fifth round. It's unclear how exactly he got the stoppage, as Barcelos, 39, appeared to lose consciousness either as he was taken down or after.

Barcelos had to be carried out of the Octagon on a stretcher, a surreal and frightening ending to what had been shaping up to be a Fight of the Year contender. He did not appear to be moving on the stretcher.

"I want everybody tonight to please pray for Raoni Barcelos. He's a warrior," Rosas said in his post-fight interview.

The UFC later reported that both fighters were being taken to the hospital for head and neck scans.

Uncrowned's Ariel Helwani has learned Barcelos regained consciousness and is able to speak and move his fingers and toes.

Barcelos' coach, Davi Ramos, released a statement echoing Helwani's report .

The UFC issued a follow-up statement late Saturday night:

Following his fight tonight, Raoni Barcelos was immediately transported to a Level 1 trauma center for evaluation. The hospital medical team conducted a CT scan and comprehensive assessment, and he is currently being monitored. Barcelos is stable, alert and responsive, with full movement. He will remain under medical supervision. We will provide updates on his condition as they become available.

The hospital medical team conducted a CT scan and comprehensive assessment, and he is currently being monitored. Barcelos is stable, alert and responsive, with full movement. He will remain under medical supervision. We will provide updates on his condition as they become available.

It had been an extremely high-paced fight, with the two fighters both throwing more than 300 total strikes, and Barcelos (22-6) logging 22 takedown attempts. All of that appeared to be part of a winning effort, as Barcelos dominated the second and the fourth rounds and was leading by multiple points on all three scorecards heading into the fifth round . Barcelos even earned a 10-8 score in the fourth round on one judge's scorecard.

Rosas (13-1) needed a finish to extend his winning streak to six wins. He got it, but we can only hope it didn't come at the cost of something serious for Barcelos.

Uncrowned will continue to update this story as information becomes available.

articles.title: Jokin García se proclama Campeón de Europa de peso ligero
articles.standfirst: Se impuso en una intensa y disputada pelea al púgil Salvi Jiménez
articles.summary: Se impuso en una intensa y disputada pelea al púgil Salvi Jiménez
articles.body: El boxeador bilbaíno Jokin García logró este sábado el cinturón de Campeón de Europa del peso ligero, tras imponerse en una intensa y disputada pelea al púgil vallisoletano Salvi Jiménez. En la velada disputada en el pabellón de La Casilla en Bilbao, Jokin 'The Hunter' García fue de nuevo profeta en su tierra, ya que hace apenas seis meses también conquistó en el mismo escenario el Europeo EBU Silver, derrotando al italiano Gianluca Ceglia. En el estelar de la cita bilbaína, ambos peleadores salieron a por todas desde el primer momento, sin esconder sus cartas. En el segundo asalto, Salvi Jiménez conectó un duro golpe que mandó a García a la lona. El vallisoletano llevó la iniciativa y tomó ventaja, dando sensación de superioridad. No fue hasta el quinto cuando Jokin García se recuperó física y anímicamente. Comenzó a meter buenas manos, algo que levantó al animoso y entregado público local. Al ecuador del combate se llegó con las espadas en todo lo alto y nada decidido. A medida que ambos boxeadores empezaron a acusar el notable esfuerzo físico, la pelea fue también al alza, con Jokin García metiendo buenas manos al rostro de Jiménez e igualando el nivel que ofrecía su adversario. Ambos acabaron exhaustos y creyéndose ganadores. Finalmente, García se proclamó vencedor a los puntos por un muy ajustado margen, discutido también desde algunos sectores del público: 111-116, 116-111, y 115-112. Tras este triunfo, el balance del púgil vizcaíno es de 15 victorias, ocho de ellas por KO, dos derrotas y un combate nulo. La velada, organizada por Kamikaze Promotions y PCI Promotions junto a Boxing Management, en colaboración con la Diputación Foral de Bizkaia, se completó con otro buen ramillete de combates previos. En los campeonatos neoprofesionales de Euskadi, Peio Gutiérez derrotó a Aritza Brazo y Gilen Obarzabal se impuso a Jon Arce. El combate entre Carlos Barbosa y Elkin Molero acabó siendo declarado nulo. Además, el guipuzcoano Rainel Ortega venció por KO a Anderson Rangel. En féminas, la británica Shona Larkman también venció a la serbia Diana Paulik en el primer asalto.

articles.title: Raoni Barcelos 'stable' in hospital after losing consciousness in defeat by Raul Rosas Jr
articles.summary: Raoni Barcelos was taken to a Las Vegas trauma centre after collapsing in the fifth round of his first UFC main event; the UFC says the 39-year-old is alert and responsive following a CT scan; Raul Rosas Jr did not celebrate and asked everybody to 'pray' for his opponent after the fight
articles.body:
The 39-year-old went down under a Rosas takedown 1:38 into the fifth round and did not get up. Medical staff attended to him inside the cage at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas before he left on a stretcher.

Rosas immediately signalled to the referee to wave off the fight.

The UFC said in a statement: "Following his fight tonight, Raoni Barcelos was immediately transported to a Level 1 trauma center for evaluation.

"The hospital medical team conducted a CT scan and comprehensive assessment, and he is currently being monitored.

"Barcelos is stable, alert and responsive, with full movement. He will remain under medical supervision."

Barcelos has been on the UFC roster since 2018 and arrived on a five-fight winning run, headlining for the first time.

The Brazilian had been in front on every card with one round left but Rosas Jr took the victory following his collapse from what looked to be a fairly innocuous takedown.

The 21-year-old has now won six successive fights, after an encounter where both men threw more than 300 strikes apiece before the ending, as the bout took the Fight of the Night bonus.

Rosas Jr muted his celebrations when he realised Barcelos' condition, and said after the fight: "I want everybody tonight to please pray for Raoni Barcelos. He's a warrior."
